newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST-Australian General News- Oct 14.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST-Australian General News- Oct 14.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN FINANCIAL REVIEW

As Prime Minister John Howard accepted the resignation of Assistant Treasurer Jim Short yesterday, Treasurer Peter Costello is under attack from the Opposition after it learned his wife holds about 200 Commonwealth Bank shares. Page 1.

Following the resignation of Jim Short, former Fraser government adviser and former Institute of Public Affairs head Rod Kemp will take up the position of assistant treasurer. Kemp, manager of government business in the Senate, was
considered unlucky to miss out on a ministry after the election. Page 4.

Although Labor is expected to back a Greens move to disallow new export woodchip regulations, the Australian Democrats will decide today whether to support Greens Senator Bob Brown's motion. The Democrats said they would not be influenced by Primary Industries Minister John Anderson, who approved another five export licenses last week, representing 40 percent of the new quota for 1996. Page 2.

An era of complete right-wing control of the New South Wales Liquor Trades Union that stretches back to the 1970s has ended, with the surprise defeat of secretary Peter James by bar employee and union delegate Sue McGrath in a union election ballot. McGrath said she would fight an Industrial Relations Commission decision last month which reduced weekend penalty rates and cut casual loadings. Page 4.
THE AUSTRALIAN

The Coalition Government has suffered a setback after Assistant Treasurer Jim Short resigned because of a breach of the Prime Minister's code of ministerial conduct. As it was announced Short would be replaced by Victorian Senator Rod Kemp, secretary to the Treasurer Brian Gibson declared he would sell his shares in the National Australia Bank and the Bank of Melbourne. Page 1.

Outspoken Queensland Independent MP Pauline Hanson is becoming increasingly isolated over her views on immigration, race and Aboriginal affairs, with Prime Minister John Howard describing her remarks as "silly" and "uninformed" and Opposition Leader Kim Beazley calling them "loopy". Page 3.

Three men were charged with drug offences in Melbourne yesterday after officers from the Australian Federal Police, the National Crime Authority, the Victorian Police and the Australian Customs Service seized 24 kg of heroin with an estimated street value of between A$25 and A$30 million on the
weekend. The arrests ended a six-month investigation by the AFP and the NCA. Page 3.

Prime Minister John Howard will meet with the commissioners investigating the separations of Aboriginal children from their families later this week, as Australian Democrats Leader Cheryl Kernot accuses the federal government of undermining the inquiry beause it fears possible compensation claims. Page 3.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

Assistant Treasurer Jim Short has resigned following the discovery of documents showing he had approved an operating licence for an ANZ Bank subsidiary while he was holding shares in the company. The approval made it impossible for Prime Minister John Howard to maintain his support for Short over his ownership of the shares. Page 1.

Darwin doctor Phillip Nitschke, the doctor who assisted in the world's first legal mercy killing, has flown to the United Kingdom to appear on a TV trial to explain why Margaret Sedgwick, a 31-year-old English mother of three who suffers from
motor neurondisease, would be allowed to end her life. Page 1.

The New South Wales government plans to introduce environment taxes, penalties and bonds, in an attempt to encourage private landholders to protect the native wildlife on their properties. The measures will also include a full audit of urban bushland and a review of the controls over the ownership of native birds. Page 3.

Scientists at the Monash Medical School at the Alfred Hospital in Melbourne are growing and culturing the skin of six-year-old Tjandamurra O'Shane, who was doused with petrol and set alight in the yard of his Cairns school last week. The boy is in a stable but serious condition in Brisbane's Royal Children's Hospital, suffering burns to 70 percent of his body. Page 3.
THE AGE

In the first casualty of the Howard ministry, Assistant Treasurer Jim Short resigned yesterday after admitting he approved a banking licence for the ANZ Banking Group while owning its shares. The affair will see the federal opposition focus on other senior figures' share interests in parliament this week. Page A1.

John Doyle and Greig Pickhaver, better known as Roy Slaven and H.G. Nelson, are set to become Australia's latest showbiz exports to Britain, with Foster's using the duo in a series of television and radio advertisements premiering this week to
promote the ber and Australian culture to the Brits. Page A1.

A study of 3,000 women by the National Health and Medical Research Council's National Breast Cancer Centre has shown many women are confused about the role age and family history can play in breast cancer. Centre director Sally Redman said that whileawareness of breast cancer was high, there were significant gaps in women's knowledge about breast cancer. Page A3.

After acknowledging that the decision to end the pursuit of runaway entrepreneur Christopher Skase was justified under existing legislation, federal cabinet will look to overhaul the bankruptcy legislation next week. It is understood that cabinet will today consider an urgent recommendation to rewrite guidelines for bankruptcy investigations. Page A3.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2
